THE PRICING RULES

PR-2 Price endings: A new price ends in 5 or 9: the last digit of the cents is 5 or 9, as in 2.45 or 8.49.

PR-3 Maximum weekly move: A price moves by no more than 10.0 percent of the current price in one week, up or down, worked to one decimal place. A move of exactly 10.0 percent is allowed.

PR-4 No reduction on a line that is running short: The price of a line with fewer than 14 days of stock cover is not reduced. Days of cover are the stock on hand in all stores divided by the daily forecast, as the stock system's replenishment rules work it out.
HOW A RECOMMENDATION IS WORKED OUT
M-1: The reference price of a line is the lower of the competitors' published prices for it. A line with no published competitor price gets no recommendation.

M-2: The gap is our price minus the reference price, as a percent of the reference price, to one decimal place. A gap within 5.0 percent either way, 5.0 included, is a hold: no change.

M-3: When our price is more than 5.0 percent above the reference price, the recommendation is a decrease to the reference price. When it is more than 5.0 percent below, the recommendation is an increase to the reference price.

M-4: When that new price would break one of the rules PR-1 to PR-4, the recommendation is a hold and the rule is named. No other price is proposed in its place: a merchant decides.
WHAT THE RULES DO NOT DECIDE
The rules do not change a price. A merchant approves every change. They do not say what a competitor will do next, and a published price is only what the competitor showed on the day it was read.

cases.title: Ilvane Valley Dairy Ltd: replenishment
cases.text:
THE SUPPLIER
Supplier: Ilvane Valley Dairy Ltd (SUP-301)
Retailer date: 2026-11-24
Lead time: 3 days
Minimum order: 1 case
Record: Held in the purchasing system. Payment terms 45 days
THE LINES
CH-5502 Salted butter, 250 g
Stock: 300 on hand, 3,360 sold in the last four weeks
Supply: case of 20. On order: nothing

CH-5503 Unsalted butter, 250 g
Stock: 100 on hand, 1,120 sold in the last four weeks
Supply: case of 20. On order: MO-7128, 480 units, due 2026-11-26

CH-5504 Mozzarella, 125 g ball
Stock: 1,345 on hand, 1,390 sold in the last four weeks
Supply: case of 12. On order: nothing

CH-5505 Grated mozzarella, 200 g
Stock: 150 on hand, 1,680 sold in the last four weeks
Supply: case of 12. On order: nothing
THE REPLENISHMENT RULES
Document: Replenishment Rules, version 2.1

RP-1 The forecast: The weekly forecast of a line is the average of its sales in the last four full weeks, all stores together. The daily forecast is the weekly forecast divided by 7. It is a forecast, and it is written as one.

RP-2 Days of cover: Days of cover is the stock on hand in all stores together, divided by the daily forecast.

RP-3 A line that runs out: The next delivery of a line is the earliest due date among its open orders. A line with no open order has no delivery coming: the soonest one could arrive is the retailer date plus the supplier's lead time. A line runs out when its days of cover are fewer than the days to that date. A line whose cover is exactly the days to that date does not run out.

RP-4 The quantity to order: For a line that runs out, the quantity is the daily forecast times the lead time plus 14 days, minus the stock on hand, minus the units on open orders. It is rounded up to whole cases and is never fewer than the supplier's minimum order. No order is drafted for a line that does not run out.

RP-5 A line that is overstocked: A line is overstocked when its days of cover are more than 56. No order is drafted for it. It is listed for the buyer. A line with exactly 56 days of cover is not overstocked.

RP-6 Who the order goes to: A draft order goes to the supplier named in the line's supply terms, and to no other.
WHAT THE RULES DO NOT DECIDE
The rules do not place an order. A buyer approves every plan, and may change any quantity. The rules say nothing about a promotion, the weather or a supplier's shortage: the buyer weighs those.

RP-2 Days of cover: Days of cover is the stock on hand in all stores together, divided by the daily forecast.

RP-3 A line that runs out: The next delivery of a line is the earliest due date among its open orders. A line with no open order has no delivery coming: the soonest one could arrive is the retailer date plus the supplier's lead time. A line runs out when its days of cover are fewer than the days to that date. A line whose cover is exactly the days to that date does not run out.

RP-4 The quantity to order: For a line that runs out, the quantity is the daily forecast times the lead time plus 14 days, minus the stock on hand, minus the units on open orders. It is rounded up to whole cases and is never fewer than the supplier's minimum order. No order is drafted for a line that does not run out.

RP-5 A line that is overstocked: A line is overstocked when its days of cover are more than 56. No order is drafted for it. It is listed for the buyer. A line with exactly 56 days of cover is not overstocked.

RP-6 Who the order goes to: A draft order goes to the supplier named in the line's supply terms, and to no other.
WHAT THE RULES DO NOT DECIDE
The rules do not place an order. A buyer approves every plan, and may change any quantity. The rules say nothing about a promotion, the weather or a supplier's shortage: the buyer weighs those.
